data.narrative:
HLabs is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Paul Hetherington that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 8 private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, plus 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the private peer set includes only a narrow band of directly comparable companies at similar stage and valuation tier.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised ($5M) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $12M. Peer-median analysis could not be applied: while 8 robotics peers exist in the broader sector, the filtered set meeting stage, adjacent-stage, and valuation-tier criteria contained fewer than the three datapoints needed for statistical reliability. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce material noise.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This relatively narrow band reflects the stage-progression method's mechanistic application rather than robust multi-method convergence. Key uncertainties include the thinness of the private comparable set at seed stage, the relevance of the single public comparable, and whether the 2.5x multiplier reflects HLabs' specific technology maturity and market positioning. Additional data on revenue run-rate or customer traction would strengthen conviction in this range.
